messages:
maya_support: @kevin_runtime FYI escalating an AcmeCorp support case — their prod jobs hitting 400 from /v1/execute-tool with 'malformed structured-args' and the function call payload ends up as a single escaped string. Customer sees retries and extra billing. Included repro and request IDs.

acme_sre: Seeing this on our side since 2026-03-15 14:05 UTC. Example request_id req_0a1b2c3d, account acme-456. We send Content-Type: application/json, model: rwd-infer-1, and tool schema expects {\"user_ids\": [\"string\"], \"action\": \"string\"}. But runtime error: 'expected array' and the function receives \"[\\\"u1\\\",\\\"u2\\\"]\" as string.

maya_support: Repro curl below — customer pasted this exact body:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/execute-tool \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{
    \"model\": \"rwd-infer-1\",
    \"tool\": \"bulk_action\",
    \"args\": {\"user_ids\":\"[\\\"u1\\\", \\\"u2\\\"]\", \"action\":\"suspend\"}
  }'
```

kevin_runtime: That looks like args.user_ids are being double-encoded client-side. Two paths: client sends stringified array, or runtime's structured-json parsing coerces arrays to strings when request is proxied. Can you attach x-request-id and raw proxy logs? Also what SDK version is customer on?

acme_sre: SDK v0.9.1 via node. x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Attaching proxy log excerpt:

```text
[2026-03-15T14:05:12Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d path=/v1/execute-tool auth=ok body_len=512 proxied=true raw_body={\"model\":\"rwd-infer-1\",\"tool\":\"bulk_action\",\"args\":{\"user_ids\":\"[\\\"u1\\\",\\\"u2\\\"]\",\"action\":\"suspend\"}}
[2026-03-15T14:05:12Z] validator=tool-schema check=fail field=args.user_ids error=expected array got string
```

ryan_eng: Agree looks like client sends stringified array. But we've seen a different bug where the request body was re-serialized by the edge when Content-Type absent or set to text/plain. Customer used application/json though. Ask: do they use any proxy or middleware that may stringify nested fields? Also check for Content-Type header case and sdk's fetch wrapper.

maya_support: Customer says hitting this intermittently; same job sometimes succeeds. They run a retry loop that re-sends the original payload (not changing it). Billing: they're billed for each retry; need a fix or mitigation ASAP.

olivia_se: Short-term mitigation: server-side validation can accept stringified arrays by attempting JSON.parse on string fields for fields declared array in schema. Not ideal but reduces customer impact. Long-term: we must ensure request body passes through unmodified.

kevin_runtime: Quick ask: eng-runtime team, add a logging hook to print the type of args before validator and include header map for failing requests. If we can reproduce locally I'll try to track reserialization in proxy layer. Also, can someone confirm whether our request canonicalization step (pkg:body-normalizer) has a fallback that turns unknown structured types into strings when header is duplicated?

ryan_eng: I'll reproduce with node SDK v0.9.1 and with raw curl. If curl sends array properly and sdk doesn't, we can patch sdk. If curl also trips the issue via the same edge route, runtime is culprit.

maya_support: Action items:
- acme_sre: share full request chain and any middleware code
- ryan_eng: reproduce and confirm SDK vs curl
- kevin_runtime: add debug logs on edge to capture raw bytes for req_0a1b2c3d timeframe
- olivia_se: implement temporary tolerant parser in validator and coordinate deploy window

support-bot: deployment window scheduled 2026-03-16T02:00 UTC for validator tolerant parse (canary 10%).

acme_sre: Thank you — please keep us posted. Their SLA impacted by retries.

kevin_runtime: I'll update thread after logs ingested. In the meantime, if anyone sees similar customer reports, ping here. :thumbsup:
